prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semester according to the study plan

learning_outcomes.text: Students have received an introduction to forming technology and knowledge of the theoretical fundamentals. They are thus able to answer fundamental questions, based on an understanding of tribological and material-technical relationships in forming technology, by using material models.
Students know the most important forming processes, their underlying characteristics, and typical applications.

Students can select suitable forming processes for concrete forming technology problems and evaluate them based on their properties, such as economic efficiency, accuracy, and environmental compatibility.
Special skills are acquired in the area of plasticity theory, deep drawing, and the determination of characteristic values (tensile test, cupping test).
Students receive an introduction and fundamental knowledge of machining technology.
Students also know the most important processes, their operating methods, fundamental characteristics, and typical applications.
Students also receive an overview of the most important cutting tools, cooling and lubrication, and common machine tools.

Students can select suitable machining processes, cutting tools, and corresponding machine tools for specific manufacturing technology problems and classify them based on their properties, such as economic efficiency, accuracy, and environmental impact.
Special competencies are acquired in the area of surface setting during turning, milling, and grinding.

syllabus_topics: Plasticity theory; material models and laws
Bulk forming - flow and piece goods
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination. The module examination can be a written exam (180-240 minutes) or an oral exam (45-60 minutes). In the exam, students should be able to select, sketch, and explain suitable manufacturing techniques for exemplary problems. Based on theoretical comparisons or analytical calculations, students should be able to argue their selection.
